summary: Web reading tool pack, stdlib only: polite-fetch.py fills an on-disk cache with a ledger from a URL list and makes the politeness mechanical — robots.txt consulted per host before the first content request and treated as disallow when it cannot be read, a one-second floor between requests that no flag can lower, a truthful faion-web-parse User-Agent whose only variable part is the contact address, 200 requests and 120 s per host per run unless the host is one you assert you own, no cookie jar and no auth-wall circumvention, and a distinct exit code so a robots-truncated crawl can never be mistaken for a complete one. page-extract.py turns that cache into readable text or markdown plus JSON-LD, OpenGraph and microdata in one pass per page, writing JSONL to a file so raw HTML never reaches the model, and it fixes the bug that quietly breaks every hand-rolled html.parser scraper: HTMLParser fires no end tag for an implied one, so unclosed li and p elements corrupt the depth stack and mis-nest structured data on most real pages. Contact fields are never emitted and emails in prose are redacted.
